chunks: And with this chain, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that he said:

I can foresee the palaces set up beside the shrine of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). It is as if many carriages have set out from Kufa towards the shrine of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Not before a few days and nights have passed will they set out towards him, and this is at the end of the era of the Umayyads.
ai.seo_question: What did Ali ibn Abi Talib predict about the shrine of Imam Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam Ali (a.s.) vividly describes the future transformation of Karbala into a major spiritual center, with palaces erected around Imam Husayn’s (a.s.) shrine and continuous pilgrim processions from Kufa. This prophecy is specifically linked to the decline of the Umayyad dynasty (Banu Marwan), highlighting the shift from political oppression to religious prominence for the Ahl al-Bayt. The imagery underscores the enduring legacy of the Imam of Martyrs and the establishment of his shrine as a focal point for Shia devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-190 According to the same documentation, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said,

“I can foresee the palaces set up besides the shrine of Al-Husayn (a.s.). It is as if many carriages have set out from Kufa towards the shrine of Al-Husayn (a.s.). Not before a few days and nights have passed will they set out towards him, and this is at the end of the era of the Umayyads.”
